accept.en: to agree that something is true or correct

acknowledge.en: to admit or accept that something is true or exists

admit.en: to agree, often unwillingly, that something is true

ambiguous.en: having more than one possible meaning; unclear

anonymous.en: made or done by someone whose name is not known

appoint.en: to officially choose someone for a job or position

balanced.en: giving fair and equal attention to different sides or parts

commonplace.en: ordinary and not unusual or interesting

compelling.en: very convincing or holding your attention strongly
compelling.zh: 令人信服的；引人入勝的

complex.en: made of many connected parts; difficult to understand

compose.en: to write or create something such as music or a poem; to make up

comprehensive.en: including all or nearly all parts or details

conceal.en: to hide something or keep it secret

concealed.en: hidden from view or kept secret

concede.en: to admit, often reluctantly, that something is true

consistent with.en: in agreement with or matching something

conventional.en: following accepted customs or usual ways

coordinated.en: organized so that different parts work well together

counter.en: to act against something or reduce its effect

decipher.en: to figure out the meaning of something difficult to read or understand

decode.en: to change a coded message into ordinary language; to interpret

decorative.en: meant to look attractive rather than to be useful

definitive.en: final, complete, and not able to be questioned
definitive.zh: 決定性的；權威的；最終的

delegate.en: to give part of your work or authority to someone else

deny.en: to say that something is not true

derived from.en: coming from or developed out of something

diminish.en: to make or become smaller or less important

dismiss.en: to decide that something is not worth considering

disorienting.en: making someone confused about where they are or what is happening
disorienting.zh: 使人迷惘的；令人困惑的

distant.en: far away in space or time

dormant.en: not active or growing now but able to become active later

durable.en: able to last a long time without breaking or wearing out

eclipsed by.en: made to seem less important by something greater

elusive.en: difficult to find, catch, or understand
elusive.zh: 難以捉摸的；難以理解的

equivalent to.en: equal in value, amount, meaning, or importance to

erase.en: to remove completely so no trace is left

erratic.en: not regular or predictable; changing often

essential.zh: 必要的；不可或缺的；本質的

forecast.en: to say what is likely to happen in the future

formative.en: having an important influence on the development of something
formative.zh: 形成期的；有重大影響的

functional.en: having a practical use; working as intended
functional.zh: 有功能的；實用的；能運作的

gradual.en: happening slowly over a long period

grant.en: to admit that something is true; to give or allow

imminent.zh: 即將發生的；迫在眉睫的

impartial.en: not favoring one side over another; fair

important.en: having great value, meaning, or effect

inactive.en: not doing anything; not working or functioning
inactive.zh: 不活躍的；無作用的；靜止的

independent of.en: not influenced by or relying on something

indicative of.en: serving as a sign or evidence of something

indisputable.en: so clearly true that it cannot be questioned
indisputable.zh: 無可爭辯的；無庸置疑的

inert.en: not moving or active; having no chemical or biological effect
inert.zh: 無活性的；惰性的；不動的

infer.en: to reach a conclusion based on evidence and reasoning

interpret.en: to explain or understand the meaning of something

irrelevant.en: not connected with or important to the matter at hand

irrelevant to.en: not connected with or important to something

landmark.en: marking an important stage or turning point

latent.en: present but not yet visible, active, or developed

manufacture.en: to make goods in large quantities, often with machines

measurable.en: large enough to be noticed or measured

meticulous.en: very careful and paying close attention to every detail
meticulous.zh: 一絲不苟的；極為仔細的

minor.zh: 次要的；較小的；不重要的

modeled on.en: designed or made to copy or follow something

momentous.en: very important because of its effect on the future

necessary.en: needed in order to achieve something

nuanced.en: showing subtle differences or shades of meaning

obscure.en: not well known; or difficult to understand

operative.en: working, functioning, or having an effect
operative.zh: 運作中的；有效的；起作用的

outweighed by.en: less important or influential than something else

overshadowed by.en: made to seem less important by something else

parse.en: to analyze something carefully to understand its parts and meaning

peripheral.en: not central or most important; on the edge

pivotal.en: of central importance, especially in causing change

postpone.en: to delay something until a later time

precarious.en: not secure or stable; likely to fall or fail

precipitous.en: very sudden and steep, especially a drop or decline

predict.en: to say what will happen in the future

predictable.en: happening in a way that can be expected

predictive of.en: indicating what is likely to happen

private.en: belonging to or meant for one person or group; not public

provisional.en: temporary and likely to be changed later
provisional.zh: 暫時的；臨時的；有待確認的

quiescent.en: quiet and inactive, often for a time

redundant.en: not needed because something else already does the job

refute.en: to prove that a statement or idea is wrong

reject.en: to refuse to accept or believe something

renounce.en: to formally give up a belief, claim, or right

replicable.en: able to be repeated with the same results

replicate.en: to repeat or copy something exactly, such as an experiment

replicated.en: repeated or copied exactly, often to check results

representative of.en: typical of or serving as an example of a group

require.en: to need something or make it necessary

robust.en: strong and well supported; not easily weakened

routine.en: ordinary and done regularly; not special

secretive.en: tending to hide feelings, plans, or information

speculative.en: based on guesses rather than firm evidence

subordinate to.en: lower in rank or importance than something else

subtle.en: not obvious; small and hard to notice

synchronized with.en: happening at the same time or rate as something

translate.en: to change words into another language; to interpret

unoriginal.en: not new or creative; copied from others

unpredictable.en: not able to be known or expected in advance
unpredictable.zh: 無法預測的；難以預料的

vestigial.en: remaining from an earlier stage but no longer having a useful function
vestigial.zh: 退化的；殘留的；無功能的

visible.en: able to be seen or noticed

waive.en: to choose not to require or enforce a rule or right

well-founded.en: based on good evidence or reasoning
